solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part negotiable after alteration in theatre feature

indicators.note: once altered, the letters of these two words are reshaped into a new phrase

explanation.surface: A clause in a contract is renegotiated, somehow involving a feature of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' here is the hospital kind where surgeons operate, not a playhouse; 'after alteration' rearranges PART NEGOTIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical theatre's central piece of furniture is the bed-like platform the patient lies on during surgery.

clue.text: Ham? One month has woman tucking in

indicators.note: the month tucks the woman in, holding her name between its letters

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October, one month of the year
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A query about ham, then a picture of a woman snuggled up with a month to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' is the verb, as in hamming it up, not the meat; 'One month' is a single abbreviated month name.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, which is exactly what overplaying a part means.

clue.text: Entertainment at castle — tonight a redoubt goes wild

indicators.note: the letters going wild are thrown into a fresh disorderly arrangement

explanation.surface: Tonight a fortified stronghold erupts in chaos while entertainment plays out at the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The EDINBURGH TATTOO is a famous military display held each summer on the esplanade of Edinburgh Castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh event is a spectacle of massed bands and drill staged in front of the Scottish capital's castle.

clue.text: Well-ventilated room on cattle farm having no top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a dairy is the room on a farm where milk is processed

explanation.surface: A cattle farm's room is pleasantly breezy because it has lost its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no top' drops the D from DAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with plenty of fresh air flowing through it is described as breezy or open.

clue.text: When voices may be raised sequentially

definitions.meaning: during a quarrel or argument, when people shout

explanation.surface: Voices are raised one after another, as in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part with ROW rhyming with 'cow', a noisy quarrel; the second with ROW rhyming with 'go', a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a quarrel (one pronunciation) and consecutively, in a line (the other).

clue.text: Liberal is keen to get behind Government errors

indicators.note: the liberal and the keenness come after, behind, the government in a down entry

parts.note: someone who itches to do something is keen to do it

explanation.surface: A Liberal is eager to back the Government, despite its errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitches are minor faults or malfunctions, especially in a system or machine, so they are mistakes.

clue.text: Disruptive worker is on CIA list initially

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
O is a shortened form of on
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word list only

explanation.surface: A disruptive worker has found themselves on a CIA watch list.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for 'on' (as in O-level abbreviations of words); 'initially' takes just L from 'list'.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that upsets other people and disregards social norms is unfriendly and disorderly.

clue.text: Anthem offering trade-offs with hymnal, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A national song is offered alongside compromises and a hymn book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words; LAND OF MY FATHERS is the national anthem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh national song, Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau, is known in English by this title.

clue.text: River — among six others?

indicators.note: among puts the river's letter in amid the letters of the number

parts.note: one thing plus six others makes seven in all

explanation.surface: A river counted alongside six other rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: R among six others makes seven, so R goes inside SEVEN; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn flows from Wales through western England to the Bristol Channel, so it is a waterway.

clue.text: African state: it's about to enter historic period

indicators.note: the two pieces enter, going inside the period

parts.note: an era is a historic period
IT taken as written, the 's being a link
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An African country is about to step into a historic new chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Earnest part of speech prefixed by one note

indicators.note: the grammatical piece is preceded by the other two pieces placed in front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tense is part of the grammar of speech, such as past or present

explanation.surface: An earnest grammatical lesson begins with a single musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense is loosely called a 'part of speech' here, though strictly it is a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intense is serious and passionate, which matches earnest as an adjective.

clue.text: Pop group whose comeback is like they've never been away?

indicators.text: whose comeback is like they've never been away
indicators.note: a comeback read backwards gives the same name, as though nothing had changed

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A pop group reunites and it is as though they never left.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads the same in both directions, so its 'comeback' looks unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish quartet behind Waterloo and Dancing Queen is one of pop's best-known bands.

clue.text: Criterion's where you'll see someone in As You Like It

definitions.meaning: a standard or test by which things are judged

definitions.text: someone in As You Like It
definitions.meaning: the court jester in Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It

explanation.surface: A standard set by a character from a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a benchmark, from the stone used to test gold, and is also the name of Shakespeare's clown.

clue.text: Recording allowed to pick up sound of drunk by extrasensory means?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the pieces so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a tape is a recording
let means allowed
hic is the sound of a drunk's hiccup

explanation.surface: A recording is permitted to capture a drunk's noise, perhaps by mind-reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick up' turns TAPELET into TELEPAT in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathic communication passes thoughts between minds without the five senses, which is extrasensory.

clue.text: Production that's unsuccessful contribution to Christmas festivities?

definitions.meaning: a show or film that flops badly
the bird traditionally roasted for Christmas dinner

explanation.surface: A failed show is somehow part of the Christmas celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical flop is slangily called this, and it is also the traditional festive roast bird.

clue.text: One following Queen entering female prison

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: the queen enters the prison, sitting inside it

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A follower of the Queen walks into a women's jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' is the royal abbreviation for Her Majesty, not ER; 'One following' is the definition, not a direction to place a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal follower or sidekick who carries out a boss's orders, often a heavy.

clue.text: What's found in various wet areas?

definitions.text: What's found in various wet areas?

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about what is found in a range of wet places.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and supplies the anagram of WET AREAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt water of the oceans fills marshes, estuaries and coastal areas.

clue.text: Who will be allowed in running heats?

definitions.text: Who will be allowed in running heats?

indicators.note: the word for allowed goes in, inside, the scrambled letters
running signals the letters are run into a new arrangement

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A question about who gets to take part in race heats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges the five letters as ATHES around the inserted word; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Track competitors are the people permitted to run in qualifying races.

clue.text: First to last, more wretched snakes

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the last position

parts.note: sadder means more wretched

explanation.surface: Snakes go from first to last, more wretched with each place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to last' moves the S of SADDER to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Adders are venomous vipers, the only poisonous serpent native to Britain.

clue.text: Foremen overlooking worker's latest errors

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so a letter is left out

parts.note: gaffers are foremen or bosses

indicators.note: the latest letter is the final one of the word worker

explanation.surface: Supervisors miss their worker's most recent mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' takes R from 'worker's', which 'overlooking' removes from GAFFERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffes are social blunders or embarrassing mistakes.

clue.text: Piece of music managed to be accepted by very good singer

indicators.note: the pieces are taken in, held inside the other word

parts.note: so can mean very good, as in 'that's so'
op is short for opus, a musical work
ran means managed

explanation.surface: A piece of music manages to win acceptance from a fine singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice range.

clue.text: Plaster not entirely fixed? Firm underneath

indicators.note: in a down entry the firm sits underneath the other piece
not entirely leaves the word incomplete, minus its last letter

parts.note: stuck means fixed
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Plaster that hasn't quite set, with a firm base beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used for coating walls and moulding decorations.

clue.text: Party leader in action — why wait for reshuffle — knock off

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, here of action
a reshuffle mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A party leader urges action rather than delaying for a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off someone is to kill or eliminate them, the same as getting rid of them.

clue.text: Second most important concern for organist

parts.note: top means most important

explanation.surface: An organist's second greatest worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second most important' reads as one phrase but splits into S and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ has knobs that select ranks of pipes, which the organist pulls to change the sound.

clue.text: Musician ignoring piano support

indicators.note: ignoring the piano means leaving its letter out

parts.note: a piper is a musician
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician ignores the piano's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column that supports a bridge or arch.

clue.text: Fantasy writer taking covers off tool fitment

indicators.note: the covers of the name are its outer letters, which come off

parts.note: Terry Pratchett wrote the Discworld fantasy novels

explanation.surface: A fantasy author removes the covers to fit a tool attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism fitted to spanners and screwdrivers allowing movement in one direction.

clue.text: Fancy me sitting in broken chair

indicators.note: me sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
a broken word has its letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imagines themselves sitting in a broken chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles the furniture word into CHIRA, opened after its third letter; 'Fancy' is a noun meaning a flight of imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fantasy or illusion, a creation of the imagination.

clue.text: A lot of worry also about outrageous piece of music

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: concern means worry

indicators.note: the word for also goes about, around, the other

parts.note: too means also
gross means outrageous, flagrant

explanation.surface: Plenty of worry about an outrageous composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims CONCERN to CONCER.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto grosso is a Baroque orchestral work contrasting a small group of soloists with the full ensemble.
